violation.description: Form <input> element has no associated <label>, aria-label, or aria-labelledby.
violation.root_cause: The search input element lacks an accessible name because no <label> element references it via htmlFor, and no aria-label or aria-labelledby attributes are present. The placeholder attribute provides only a visual hint and is not exposed to assistive technologies as a label.
violation.user_impact: Screen reader users cannot determine the purpose of this search field; they will hear an unlabeled 'edit text' or generic 'search' without context. Users relying on voice control or cognitive aids also lack a clear identifier for the control.
violation.fix_strategy: Add an explicit accessible name: either wrap a <label htmlFor="search-box">Search components</label> (visually hidden if design requires) or add aria-label="Search components" directly to the input element.
violation.plain_explanation: In Header.tsx, a critical priority Unlabeled Form Field issue was identified: Form <input> element has no associated <label>, aria-label, or aria-labelledby. Addressing this ensures full compliance and accessible interaction for assistive technology users.

violation.description: Non-interactive <div> with onClick must have a role, tabIndex, and keyboard handler (onKeyDown).
violation.root_cause: A generic <div> element was used as an interactive trigger with an onClick handler, but divs are not natively focusable, lack implicit button semantics, and do not respond to keyboard activation (Enter/Space). The architecture omitted role="button", tabIndex={0}, and an onKeyDown handler for keyboard events.
violation.user_impact: Keyboard-only users cannot focus or activate the menu toggle. Screen reader users receive no announcement of the element's interactive purpose or state.
violation.fix_strategy: Replace the <div> with a semantic <button> element to gain native focus, role, and keyboard handling. If a div must be retained, add role="button", tabIndex={0}, and an onKeyDown handler that triggers toggleMenu on Enter/Space.
violation.plain_explanation: In Header.tsx, a critical priority Non Interactive Click issue was identified: Non-interactive <div> with onClick must have a role, tabIndex, and keyboard handler (onKeyDown). Addressing this ensures full compliance and accessible interaction for assistive technology users.

violation.description: Form <textarea> element has no associated <label>, aria-label, or aria-labelledby.
violation.root_cause: The textarea element lacks an accessible name because no <label> element with htmlFor referencing the textarea's id was provided, nor were aria-label or aria-labelledby attributes used. Unlike the preceding email input (lines 16-22) which correctly pairs a label via htmlFor/id, the textarea's form-group (line 25) omits the label entirely, leaving only a placeholder which is not a valid accessible name per WCAG 3.3.2.
violation.affected_element: <textarea placeholder="Provide user feedback..." value={feedback} onChange={(e) => setFeedback(e.target.value)} />
violation.user_impact: Screen reader users will encounter an unlabeled text area announced only as 'edit text' or 'blank' without context, making it impossible to understand the field's purpose. Users with cognitive impairments relying on visible labels may miss the instruction since placeholders disappear on input. Keyboard-only users are unaffected directly but lose programmatic association for form navigation.
violation.fix_strategy: Add a <label htmlFor="feedback-id">Feedback</label> before the textarea and assign id="feedback-id" to the textarea, or alternatively add aria-label="Provide user feedback" directly on the textarea element.
violation.plain_explanation: In LoginForm.tsx, a critical priority Unlabeled Form Field issue was identified: Form <textarea> element has no associated <label>, aria-label, or aria-labelledby. Addressing this ensures full compliance and accessible interaction for assistive technology users.

violation.description: <button> element has no accessible text name and no aria-label.
violation.root_cause: The button element contains only a decorative icon element (<i className="icon-refresh") with no text content, aria-label, aria-labelledby, or title attribute. The icon is rendered via CSS (likely a font icon or background image) and provides no semantic information to assistive technologies.
violation.user_impact: Screen reader users will encounter a button announced only as "button" with no description of its purpose (refresh). Keyboard-only users can focus the control but receive no audible cue about its function, making the control unusable for non-visual interaction.
violation.fix_strategy: Provide an accessible name using aria-label="Refresh" on the button, and mark the icon as decorative with aria-hidden="true" on the element. Alternatively, include visually hidden text content (e.g., Refresh) inside the button.
violation.plain_explanation: The refresh button in the header relies solely on an icon with no text label, so screen readers announce it only as ‘button’ without explaining its purpose. This leaves screen reader and keyboard-only users unable to understand or use the control. To fix it, add aria-label='Refresh' to the button and mark the icon as decorative with aria-hidden='true'.

violation.description: Anchor <a> element has an empty, '#', or missing href attribute.
violation.root_cause: An anchor element (<a>) is being used as an interactive control with an onClick handler but has a placeholder href="#" and preventDefault() is called, indicating it functions as a button rather than a navigational link. This violates semantic HTML structure — anchors must have valid navigation targets, while actions should use <button> elements.
violation.user_impact: Screen reader users hear "link" announcement but activation does not navigate, causing confusion. Keyboard-only users may expect link behavior (new page, history entry) but get none. Voice control users saying "click link" may fail if the element is not recognized as a true link.
violation.fix_strategy: Replace the <a> element with a <button type="button"> element since the control triggers an action (opening docs/help) rather than navigating. Remove the href attribute entirely. Ensure the button has accessible text content ("Docs & Help" is present).
violation.plain_explanation: In Header.tsx, a critical priority Empty Link Or Button issue was identified: Anchor <a> element has an empty, '#', or missing href attribute. Addressing this ensures full compliance and accessible interaction for assistive technology users.

violation.description: Avoid positive tabIndex values (2) which disrupt natural focus navigation order.
violation.root_cause: The developer explicitly assigned tabIndex={2} to the submit button, forcing it into a specific position in the browser's focus navigation sequence that contradicts the natural DOM order of form controls (email input → password input → feedback textarea → submit button). This manual override disrupts the logical tab flow defined by the document structure.
violation.user_impact: Keyboard-only users and screen reader users will experience unpredictable focus jumps when tabbing through the form — the submit button may receive focus before preceding fields (like the feedback textarea) or be skipped entirely, breaking the expected sequential navigation and causing disorientation or missed inputs.
violation.fix_strategy: Remove the tabIndex prop entirely to restore natural DOM-order focus navigation. If visual order differs from DOM order, restructure the JSX markup to match the intended reading/tab sequence rather than using tabIndex to patch it.
violation.plain_explanation: The submit button was given a forced tab index that overrides the natural DOM order, causing keyboard and screen reader users to encounter unpredictable focus jumps and miss fields. This disruption affects users who rely on sequential tab navigation, leading to disorientation and potential input errors.

violation.description: Images must have an alt attribute describing the image or alt="" if decorative.
violation.root_cause: The element lacks an alt attribute entirely. As a company logo, this image conveys essential brand identity information, but the markup provides no text alternative for assistive technologies.
violation.user_impact: Screen reader users receive no information about the logo's content or purpose, losing critical brand context. If the logo is decorative, the missing alt attribute still causes a violation because decorative images require explicit alt="" to be properly ignored.
violation.fix_strategy: Add an alt attribute with descriptive text reflecting the logo's content (e.g., alt="Acme Corp logo") if informative, or alt="" if purely decorative. Determine intent from design context.
violation.plain_explanation: In Header.tsx, a critical priority Missing Alt Text issue was identified: Images must have an alt attribute describing the image or alt="" if decorative. Addressing this ensures full compliance and accessible interaction for assistive technology users.
